area: Flash/AS3 animation semantics for transcription (SESSION 24 A12.3: run_sheathed, death, hit reaction)

items.title: Frame-level r="1" flag exists in the payload and the transcriber silently drops it — including in already-committed balancedhorizontalslash_partc
items.claim: Probed all 158 anims in reference/extracted/bindata/108_1t4635s0.bin: <f> elements carry an undocumented r="1" attribute on 89 frames across 25 anims (heavyjumpslash_parta x6, gangnam x43, stabattack, launchopponent, ...). One of them is balancedhorizontalslash_partc frame i=5 — an anim ALREADY transcribed into src/config/ogAnims.ts with the flag silently discarded, because transcribeAnims.py's frame regex `<f i="(\d+)"[^>]*>` validates unknown attrs on <n> but swallows anything extra on <f> and <anim>. Flash-era formats have exactly this trap: the PlaceObject2 ratio field was documented as morph-only yet actually controls whether a nested Sprite's playhead resets — undocumented flags carry real playback semantics. In partc, frame 5 is a full 19-node frame so overlay-vs-reset is indistinguishable there, but a wrong guess will show in anims where the r-frame is sparse.

items.adjudication_reason: transcribeAnims.py enforces fail-loud on <n> attrs (`known = set(kv) - {...}` sys.exit) but its <f> regex `<f i="(\d+)"[^>]*>` ignores frame attrs; ogAnims.ts balancedhorizontalslash_partc therefore already lost frame 5's r="1" — the D4 'verbatim, byte-true' contract in the ogAnims.ts header is currently violated.
items.implementation_note: Extend the fail-loud grammar to <f> and <anim> attribute allowlists ({i,r} and {i,d,l}), record the flag verbatim as e.g. `refresh?: boolean` on the frame, and have OgAnimPlayer treat its semantics as an open question: plausible meanings are 'reset carried map before overlay' or a keyframe marker. Grade its behavior against video only where a sparse r-frame exists. Re-run the transcriber + byte-check suite after.

items.title: Flash Matrix column semantics (x'=a·x+c·y+tx, y'=b·x+d·y+ty) — repo's planPose already applies the exact AS3 formula, and /100 is the right divisor
items.claim: AS3 flash.geom.Matrix is [a c tx / b d ty / 0 0 1]: x'=a·x+c·y+tx, y'=b·x+d·y+ty; pure rotation is a=cos, b=sin, c=−sin, d=cos, and the SWF-native storage of these terms is 16.16 fixed-point with scale folded in (a=Sx·cos, b=Sy·sin(rotateskew0), c=−Sx·sin(rotateskew1), d=Sy·cos). The payload's x100 integers are therefore NOT a SWF or AS3 convention — they are Lut's exporter quantizing float matrices to 2 decimals. Consequence: the 2-decimal precision loss is IN THE SOURCE, so transcribing verbatim and dividing by 100 at compose time reproduces exactly what the OG engine read back; do not 'recover' precision or renormalize the quads.
items.adjudication_reason: src/core/planPose.ts Mat2 doc comment states and applies exactly 'x' = a·x + c·y, y' = b·x + d·y' with rotation as [cos, sin, −sin, cos]; src/core/composePose.ts divides all four terms by OG_MATRIX_UNITS=100 (src/config/ogPose.ts). The web-grounded AS3 formula matches the code term-for-term, including sign placement.
items.implementation_note: Nothing to change. Death's 6 matrix nodes will flow through the existing path. Keep the 'never renormalize' rule in mind if a matrix quad in death looks non-orthogonal — the OG's own quantization makes slight non-orthogonality authentic.

items.title: A12.3 targets probed byte-level: run_sheathed and death parse cleanly under the existing grammar; the whole payload has NO color transforms, motion guides, labels, or scripts
items.claim: Direct probe of 108_1t4635s0.bin: the entire 158-anim / 1638-frame / 24502-node payload contains only 4 element types (animdata, anim, f, n) and <n> carries only i,x,y,r,a,b,c,d — all integer values, no color-transform attrs, no frame labels, no scripts, no guide paths. Flash motion tweens/guides/easing are authoring-time constructs; this exporter baked everything to per-frame keys, so tween semantics never reach the transcriber. run_sheathed: d=9, l="1", 9 dense 19-node frames, rotation-only, no r-flags. death: d=38, non-looping, 38 dense 19-node frames, 6 matrix nodes, no r-flags, standard slot set (0-7, 9-16, 18-20 — same as walk/idle). Both are strictly simpler than the already-shipped balancedhorizontalslash chain (no sparse frames at all).

items.title: No dedicated 'hit reaction' clip exists in the payload — map §S24-F's three measured reactions to the gotlaunched/downed/brake clip family from video before transcribing
items.claim: The 158-name inventory has no 'hit', 'hurt', 'flinch', or 'react' clip. The reaction-shaped candidates are: gotlaunchedupwards_parta/b/c, gotlauncheddowned + gotlauncheddownedend, downed/downedup/downedup2/flipupfromdowned, brake, defeatedanimationv1/v2, and (attacker-side) launchopponent. The ledger's §S24-F measured exactly three distinct player hit reactions — knock-up LAUNCHER (~270 px vertical, lands 7 ticks), KNOCKDOWN (prone tumble, up by ~6 ticks), knockback slide (−188 px + skid) — which plausibly map to gotlaunchedupwards_*, gotlauncheddowned(+end/downedup), and brake respectively, but that mapping is unverified. Small hits (−7/−12 HP, ~0 displacement) may play NO skeleton reaction at all (hit-stop + red wash only, both engine-side per §S24-F).

items.title: deathbyarrow introduces slot 21 — the only anim beyond the 0-20 slot map; add a slot-range fail-loud before the death-variant anims
items.claim: Payload-wide probe: 157 of 158 anims stay within slots 0-20 with 8/17 absent everywhere (the transcriber's alias guard is validated against the FULL payload, not just the 4 shipped anims). The single exception is deathbyarrow, which adds slot 21 (the embedded arrow). The A12.3 'death' clip is unaffected (standard 19-slot set), but the transcriber has no upper-bound slot guard and composePose/OG_DRESSED_SLOT_SHAPES has no shape for 21 — transcribing deathbyarrow today would pass the transcriber and then throw (or silently drop) at compose time depending on the slot-map lookup path.

items.title: The 15 fps latch + carry-forward player is the correct Flash playback model — validated against Flash timeline semantics, no changes warranted
items.claim: Flash semantics confirm all three pillars of the repo's player: (1) the document frame rate is a single global clock — every nested MovieClip advances one frame per stage frame (Flash's default was 12 fps historically, 24 in later versions; a 15 fps document setting like SHS Duels' is a deliberate authoring choice, and the §S24-E 60 fps burst proof of 4-duplicate-frame content blocks confirms zero engine-side interpolation); (2) timeline objects persist at their depth across frames unless explicitly re-placed or removed — sparse frames listing only changed depths ARE the native Flash storage model, so carry-forward is fidelity, not a workaround; (3) whether a nested clip's playhead resets on re-encounter is controlled by the PARENT (the ratio-field mechanism), matching the repo's 'the a→b→c chain policy is the scene's, not the data's' split exactly.

items.adjudication_reason: src/core/ogAnimPlayer.ts implements all three: ANIM_TIMING.poseStepMs whole-step latch (matching ledger §S24-E's 'pure 15 fps stepper, zero interpolation' burst proof), the `carried` Map overlay contract documented in its header with the measured partc example, and `advanceOne`'s hold-last-frame + caller-owned chaining; DuelScene.fighterPose owns the a→b→c policy.
items.implementation_note: Nothing to change. For death (non-loop, d=38) the existing hold-last-frame behavior is also OG-correct: §S24-F shows the kill pose holds until the kill-cam cut, so the scene keeps the finished player parked rather than swapping to idle.

dead_ends: No documentation exists anywhere for Lut Games' custom animdata XML grammar (the DefineBinaryData payload is their own exporter format — the x100 quantization and the frame-level r flag are ungoogleable; grounded them by probing the bindata directly instead). Searched for Ruffle-specific docs on sparse-keyframe carry-forward — nothing direct beyond the SWF spec's PlaceObject2 move semantics. No SHS Duels technical postmortem or Explosive Barrel dev blog surfaced in any search. The moldstud/animationclub frame-rate results were content-farm grade and discarded; kirupa retained only for the Flash-default history claim it actually supports.
